newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka tea prices down on cooling demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka tea prices down on cooling demand.

text.p: Tea prices fell at the Colombo auction on Wednesday as demand for the 5.4 million kg on offer was low with major buyers having already concluded their purchases ahead of the upcoming holiday season, brokers said.

Demand from the Commonwealth of Indepedent States (CIS), which sent prices soaring to record levels in recent months, was restricted with required quantities already having reached their destinations before winter, they added.
"Its a seasonal phenomenon. Buyers should be back for more quantities after the holiday season," said Rohan Iddawela of brokers Forbes and Walker.

All high grown teas -- except for better western BOPs, which appreciated four to six rupees -- fell two to eight rupees. Low growns too declined in value except for some stylish leafy grades, which appreciated substantially, Iddawela said.
Demand came from Britain, Japan and South Africa in the absence of much CIS activity, brokers said.
Brokers Forbes said the anticipated gross auction average fell to 102 rupees ($1.79) per kg against 105.77 last week.
The next auction is on November 26-27 where 5.3 million kg will be on offer. ($1=Rs.56.94)
